name: CROR Trainer — Grande Prairie
statusNote: A content source superseded at parity by Clear Board — its rule bank, radio steps, and signal renderer live on there — but kept live on its own page.
oneLiner: A browser-based trainer for CN freight-conductor skills — rule recall, switch-list reading, yard switching, signals, and radio walkthroughs — modeled on a real CN yard.
stack: Vanilla JavaScript/HTML, zero build step, zero dependencies
Each module a single self-contained .html file
Offline dev tooling only: Node checks, a BFS puzzle solver, Python + OpenCV for the yard-map trace

components.name: index.html hub
components.desc: A card-grid launcher in a hub-and-spoke layout.

components.name: CROR Quiz
components.desc: Data-driven quiz, ~325 questions in escalating tiers; every answer cites a rule number.

components.name: GP Switching Puzzle
components.desc: A state-model switching puzzle with offline-BFS-verified par solutions.

components.name: GP Switching Sim
components.desc: A newer canvas prototype, spun into its own standalone repo.

components.name: GP Yard Board
components.desc: A clickable yard map traced from a real photo via OpenCV homography.

components.name: GP Radio Steps
components.desc: A guided radio-call walkthrough with locked wording.

components.name: Signal Reading
components.desc: An SVG signal renderer covering ~102 hardware forms across 38 of 42 indications.

dataFlow: The official rulebook PDF (gitignored, never redistributed) is parsed offline, then hand-authored into the question bank.
The quiz orders questions in escalating tiers; every answer shows its citation and collects misses for an end-of-run review.
Switching puzzles replay a composed move list against the track state, animating each step.
Wins are graded on correctness and efficiency against an offline-precomputed par.
integrations: Official CROR PDF and a third-party study aid — gitignored source material, never redistributed
Yard geometry traced from a real 2020 CN Grande Prairie diagram via OpenCV
decisions: A verbatim safety rule in its docs: never guess or infer rule content.
Rulebook rules and company operating practice are kept strictly distinguishable.
Never republish the official rulebook itself.
Yard geometry must come from the processed photo trace — three hand-drawn attempts were rejected as topologically wrong.
Radio-call wording is locked by a subject-matter expert.
Every puzzle is machine-verified solvable before it ships.
